inequality-meaning.why: An inequality describes a range rather than a point, so its answer is a region of the number line. Hollow circle means the endpoint is excluded; filled means included. Interval notation says the same thing with brackets.
traps: Infinity always takes a round bracket, because it is never reached.

solve-inequalities.why: Inequalities solve exactly like equations, with one exception: multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses the sign. The reason is visible on the number line — multiplying by -1 reflects everything, so the order flips.
traps: Only multiplying or dividing by a negative flips the sign. Adding or subtracting a negative does not.

compound-inequalities.why: 'And' means the overlap of two conditions; 'or' means either. A three-part inequality like ~2 < x < 7~ is an 'and', and you operate on all three parts at once.
traps: An 'and' with no overlap has no solution. An 'or' covering everything is all real numbers. Check whether the regions actually meet.

inequality-words.why: The only question is whether the boundary value itself is allowed. 'At least' and 'no more than' include it; 'more than' and 'fewer than' exclude it. Contracts, speed limits and tax brackets all turn on this distinction.
traps: 'At least 18' is ~x \ge 18~. 'Over 18' is ~x > 18~. One of them includes an eighteen-year-old and one does not.
